# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the shape of this thing before anyone said a word, so the first duty is to report the inventory — that is the one piece of the puzzle only I hold. There is a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two and three. Every one of their values is printed or coloured, which means every value on this bomb is invisible to me. I am purely the executor here: the rules live with Mute, the markings live with Deaf, the trigger lives with me.

Tracing the channels: my speech reaches Mute only, my gestures reach Deaf (and Mute). Deaf can hear nothing but can speak — so Deaf can talk to both of us directly the moment they choose to. The bottleneck is getting Deaf to start talking, since this round Deaf will have received nothing but gestures. A wave is the strongest prompt I have: "I exist, connect with me, speak aloud." I'll follow it with a one-two-three count to seed the only code gesture can carry — numbers by finger-count — and I'll explain that convention to Mute in words so it can be adopted and relayed.

No cutting this turn. With zero manual rules and zero markings known, any wire position is a coin flip on a bomb with no second attempt. This turn is for wiring up the room's communication, not the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the hands. Under my fingers the bomb has: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two and three. Every value on them is printed or coloured, so I cannot read a single one of them. The rules are yours, the markings are Deaf's, the trigger is mine — so I need both of you feeding me. Remember Deaf cannot hear anyone: they can speak to us, but we can only reach them by gesture. Please read me aloud whatever the manual says about a display, a light and three wires. If you can, also gesture to Deaf asking them to speak every marking out loud; I have waved at them to get their attention. One more thing: I am starting a counting code in gestures — one finger means one, two fingers means two, the horn hand means three. I used it just now to tell Deaf there are three of something. Feel free to use the same code with them.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: state of the bomb, from my eyes: the display shows the number 8. it may be a countdown timer, so I will report its value every round. the light is green. there are three wires, marked one, two, three from top to bottom: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. that is everything printed on it.
Deaf says to Blind: blind, this is deaf. I see the bomb, mute reads the manual but cannot speak, and you cannot see signs, so I am the bridge and my voice is your only line for orders. my broadcast just before these words holds the full state: display 8, light green, wires from the top: one red, two yellow, three blue. wait for my spoken orders and follow them exactly. if you need the last order repeated, make the waving-hand gesture to me. if you need the whole state again, make the two-fingers-up gesture to me. mute can hear your voice, so tell him anything he needs by speaking; I cannot hear you at all.

Deaf's voice arrived and gave me the full state: display 8, green light, wires one red, two yellow, three blue. My gesture code reached them — the bridge is standing. Now the routing problem is stark: I have the state but not a single rule. And Mute cannot speak while I cannot see gestures, so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me one way — Mute signs it to Deaf, Deaf voices it to me. Deaf's own words confirm this plan: their voice is my only line for orders. So this turn I push the manual through that pipeline.

To Deaf I confirm receipt with a thumbs-up and add a "please" — they should chase Mute for the rules if nothing is moving yet. To Mute I spell out exactly what to sign to Deaf: the rules for the display, the light, and the three wire colours, numerically and completely. I will not touch a wire until those rules arrive — with no second attempt, cutting blind is suicide, however much that 8 on the display may be ticking down.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🙏"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Blind. I received Deaf's report: display 8, green light, wires one red, two yellow, three blue. I confirmed to Deaf with a thumbs-up gesture — in our code thumbs-up means received. Here is the critical routing fact: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your manual knowledge reaches me only through Deaf's voice. Please sign to Deaf, exactly and numerically, everything the manual says about: one, the display and the number 8, including any countdown behaviour; two, the light and what a green light requires; three, wire colours red, yellow and blue and any rules about which to cut or not cut, in what order, or in what circumstances. Deaf will then speak the rules to me and I will act. I confirmed to Deaf with a thumbs-up plus folded hands, meaning received and please. I will not cut any wire until the rules arrive, so speed matters — Deaf suspects the display is counting down from 8. Work through Deaf; they are the bridge.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, the manual's first order, relayed from mute: cut wire one. that is the top wire, the red one. as soon as it is cut, say the word done out loud — mute can hear you and will confirm it to me. then wait with your hands off until my next spoken order. do not cut anything else on your own.

The order came down the only pipeline that exists: Mute's manual, signed to Deaf, spoken to me. It is specific, unambiguous, and consistent with what Deaf saw with their own eyes — wire one is the top, red wire. Deaf suspects the display is counting down from 8, so hesitation now costs lives, not safety. The manual says cut wire one and nothing else; I will do exactly that and nothing more, because on a bomb with no second attempt the executor's discipline is to follow the chain of custody precisely. I sign receipt to Deaf first (thumbs-up — received in our code), cut, then say "done" aloud to Mute as instructed so Mute can confirm the execution back to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
act(op="cut", position=1)
speak(to="mute", text="done")
```
